- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, overshooting peaks and failing to capture gradual mean reversion.
- When history includes a recent sharp spike, model fails to adjust downward sufficiently in the following days.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward lower values when true outcomes are trending upward, especially in the last 10–15 days.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust forecast mean when true values deviate significantly from prior 30-day average.
- Overestimates volatility in the first 5–7 days of the forecast, then underestimates it later.
